newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm but profit-taking seen ahead.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm but profit-taking seen ahead.

text.p: Optimism on Wall Street, combined with hopes that local interest rates will soon fall, pushed Chilean blue chip stocks almost one percent higher by the close of trading Monday, said traders.
The market is expected to open weaker Tuesday amid a wave of profit-taking, they said.
"There could be an adjustment in the short-term, but the long-term outlook is still bright," said one dealer.
The 40-share IPSA index ended up 0.93 percent at 101.95 points. The general IGPA index gained 0.62 percent to 5561.94 points.
Despite the rally, turnover remained light with volume of 8.8 billion pesos.
"There were a lot of buy orders but no sellers," said one trader.

Investors were speculating that interest rates could fall before the year-end with the talk bolstered by new figures pointing to a slowing of Chile's robust economic growth as the result of the central bank's credit-tightening, said dealers.
Data from the Sofofa trade association showed industrial output fell 0.4 percent in August from July, with sales dropping 2.5 percent.
Gainers included power generator Chilgener, up 1.79 percent at 2,555 pesos, Telex, up 1.71 percent at 1,190 pesos, and electric utility Endesa, which firmed 1.13 percent at 268 pesos.
Losers included airline LanChile, down 4.35 percent at 550 pesos, and bottler Andina, which shed 0.21 percent at 2,375 pesos.
